title: Mathematical Operations
body:
[[Binary Operations]]

What the [[ALU]] can actually do, which is less than you would like. Addition is the
primitive; everything else is built on it.

- **Add** is a chain of full adders, one per bit, carry rippling left. See
  [[Combinational Logic]].
- **Subtract** is add-the-two's-[[Complements|complement]], so no separate subtractor
  exists. `sub` and `neg` are the instructions.
- **Multiply and divide** exist on the 68000 (`muls`/`mulu`, `divs`/`divu`, signed and
  unsigned variants) but are slow, take many clock cycles, and are size-restricted:
  `mulu` is word × word into a longword, `divu` is longword ÷ word.
- **Multiply or divide by a power of two** is a shift, and is the fast path. `lsl #3`
  multiplies by 8 in one instruction; that is a [[Binary Operations|bitwise]] trick, not
  arithmetic hardware.
- **Floating point** is not here at all. The bare 68000 has no FPU, so real numbers are
  library code or a separate 68881 coprocessor.

Every operation sets the [[Status Bits]] as a side effect, and those are how you find out
that a result overflowed rather than getting an error. The hardware wraps silently; noticing
is your job.
